text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 4% today as oil prices dropped on easing Middle East tensions. Yesterday's news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts reduced fears of supply disruptions that had pushed crude up the day before; U.S. oil fell from levels near $105 back toward $103 a barrel today. For a refiner, lower crude prices sound good in theory, but the sharp reversal in just two days—climbing 10% on Wednesday's conflict fears, then reversing Thursday—whipsaws margins and creates uncertainty about what refineries can actually lock in as profit.

The bigger picture is volatility. Over two weeks, the stock has swung wildly with geopolitical headlines rather than any shift in refining fundamentals; refineries are still running at a healthy 92.8% capacity, and storage levels remain balanced. The real driver has been oil-price swings tied to Iran tensions, not the company's operations.
